title: Explicit-profile ceiling: eight-H17 standalone completion fails for .0033 <= C < 1
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Prove one abstract fixed-profile ceiling: a completion independently paying eight whole H17 jobs fails its necessary moment test for **every `.0033<=C<1`**, even granting all 240 currently unearned H25 targets, free other decoder work, no target losses and no additional route cost. The paid lower bound is `{1:6611,2:1236,3:1530,4:381,5:120,8:8}`; the helper upper bound is `{4:84,7:21,8:117,9:954}`, plus the hypothetical `240 H25`. Any larger paid profile or smaller target allowance remains covered.

At C=.0033 the raw optimistic margin is below 43, while an elementary binomial inequality makes the eight declared tails cost more than 128 at that anchor, leaving margin below −85. Pairing eight H25 terms with eight H17 costs and normalizing by 6^t proves strict increase in t=1−C, extending the negative sign through all larger C<1. The anchor cost bound is not claimed near C=1. At C*=.00330007/rho=1e−9 the remaining budget below 42.525751420427386531940225 still grants unearned targets and is not κ admission. Eight additional H1 charges simply shift either budget by −8 exactly; no new power point or physical construction is claimed.

The eight-tail tariff is an explicit protocol premise. This is no universal κ/circuit barrier, rank minimality, information lower bound, fusion obstruction or completed decoder. Changed profiles, fusion/reuse, new observations and encodings remain open; the user's goal of achieved conditional κ≥.0033 remains open.
